title: Screening and Identification of Small Peptides Targeting Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptor2 using a Phage Display Peptide Library
protocol: Dissolve 1 g of tryptone, 0.5 g of yeast extract, and 0.5 g of NaCl in 100 mL of H2O.
Autoclave the solution.
Store the LB medium at 4°C.
Prepare a tetracycline stock by mixing 20 mg/mL with 1:1 ethanol:H2O.
Vortex the tetracycline stock before using.
Mix 0.5 g of IPTG and 0.4 g of X-gal in 10 mL of DMF.
Store the IPTG/X-gal solution at -20°C in the dark for one year.
Dissolve 1 g of bacto-tryptone, 0.5 g of yeast extract, 0.5 g of NaCl, and 1.5 g of agar in 100 mL of H2O for LB + Tetracycline plates.
Autoclave the solution.
Cool to <70°C.
Add 100 μL of tetracycline stock to the cooled solution.
Pour plates.
Store the LB + Tet plates at 4°C in the dark.
Dissolve 1 g of bacto-tryptone, 0.5 g of yeast extract, 0.5 g of NaCl, and 1.5 g of agar in 100 mL of H2O for LB + IPTG/X-gal plates.
Autoclave the solution.
Cool to <70°C.
Add 100 μL of IPTG/X-gal solution to the cooled solution.
Pour plates.
Store the LB + IPTG/X-gal plates at 4°C in the dark.
Dissolve 1.5014 g of glycine and 100 mg of BSA in 100 mL of H2O for Glycine-HCl buffer.
Adjust the pH to 2.2 with HCl.
Filter the solution using a 0.22 μm filter.
Store the Glycine-HCl buffer at 4°C.
Dissolve 12.11 g of Tris in 100 mL of H2O for Tris-HCl buffer.
Adjust the pH to 9.1 with HCl.
Autoclave the solution.
Store the Tris-HCl buffer at 4°C.
Dissolve 1.68 g of NaHCO3 in 200 mL of H2O and adjust the pH to 8.6 with NaOH.
Filter the coating buffer using a 0.22 μm filter and store at 4°C.
Prepare 0.1 M NaHCO3 (pH 8.6) with 5 mg/mL BSA.
Filter the blocking buffer using a 0.22 μm filter and store at 4°C.
Prepare 50 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5) with 150 mM NaCl.
Autoclave and store TBS at room temperature.
Prepare TBS with 0.05%, 0.1%, or 0.5% (v/v) Tween-20.
Filter the TBST using a 0.22 μm filter and store at room temperature.
Prepare 20% (w/v) polyethylene glycol–8000 with 2.5 M NaCl.
Autoclave and store PEG/NaCl at room temperature.
Mix 1 mL of 1 M Tris-HCl (pH8.0) and 2 mL of 50 mM EDTA (pH 8.0).
Adjust the volume to 100 mL with H2O for TE solution.
Autoclave and store TE at room temperature.
Dissolve 30 g of NaI in 50 mL of TE, pH 8.0.
Store iodide buffer at room temperature in the dark.
Dissolve 1 g of tryptone, 0.5 g of yeast extract, 0.5 g of NaCl, and 0.7 g agarin in 100 mL of H2O for top Agar.
Autoclave and dispense into 15 mL aliquots.
Store top Agar at room temperature for use.
Prepare a 10 μg/mL FGFR2 solution in coating buffer.
Add 1 mL of the prepared solution to a 35 cm² dish and swirl repeatedly until the surface is completely wet.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C with shaking.
Inoculate 5 mL of LB + Tet medium with Escherichia coli ER2738 for 5–10 hours at 37 °C with shaking.
Pour off the coating solution from the dish and add the blocking solution.
Incubate at 4 °C for at least 1 hour.
Discard the blocking solution and wash 6 times quickly with TBST (TBS + 0.05% v/v Tween-20).
Reconstitute the original phage library in 1 mL of TBST to a final concentration of 10¹¹ plaque forming units (PFU).
Add the reconstituted phage library to the coated dish and rock gently for 2 hours on a shaker at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and wash the dish 10 times with TBST (TBS + 0.05% v/v Tween-20).
Elute the bound phage by adding 1 mL of 0.2 M glycine-HCl buffer (pH 2.2) to the dish and rocking gently for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer the eluate into a sterilized microfuge tube.
Neutralize the eluate with 100 μL of 1 M Tris-HCl, pH 9.1.
Pre-warm LB + IPTG/X-gal plates for at least 1 h at 37°C before use.
Prepare 100 µL of 10-fold serial dilutions (i.e., 101, 102, 103 and 104) of the eluate in LB.
Use tips with filter cartridges to avoid contamination.
Dispense 200 µL of culture into sterilized microfuge tubes when the culture reaches mid-log phase (OD600 ≈ 0.5).
Add 10 µL of each dilution to individual microfuge tubes containing E. coli ER2738 culture.
Vortex quickly and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Coat 90 μL of the mixture into LB + IPTG/X-gal plates with coating sticks.
Transfer the mixture to culture tubes containing 45°C top agar.
Mix quickly and immediately pour the culture onto pre-warmed LB/IPTG/X-gal plate.
Tilt and rotate the plate to spread the top agar evenly.
Invert and incubate plates overnight at 37°C.
Count plaques on plates with approximately 100 plaques.
Multiply each number by the dilution factor for that plate to get the phage titer in PFU per 10 µL.
Inoculate another 5 mL of LB + Tet medium with E. coli ER2738 at 37 °C overnight with shaking.
Dilute (1:100) the overnight culture from step 3.8 in 20 mL of LB in a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Add the unamplified eluate and incubate with vigorous shaking for 4.5 h at 37 °C.
Transfer the culture to a centrifuge tube and centrifuge for 10 min at 12,000 x g at 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube.
Centrifuge again and discard the pellet.
Transfer the upper 80% of the supernatant to a fresh tube.
Add 1/6 volume of 20% PEG/2.5 M NaCl to the supernatant.
Allow the phage to precipitate at 4 °C overnight.
Centrifuge the precipitated phage at 12,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.
Centrifuge again.
Remove the residual supernatant with a pipette.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of TBS.
Transfer the supernatant to a microfuge tube.
Centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh microfuge tube.
Add 1/6 volume of 20% PEG/2.5 M NaCl to precipitate proteins.
Incubate on ice for 15–60 min.
Centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.
Re-spin and remove residual supernatant with a pipette.
Resuspend the pellet in 200 μL of TBS.
Centrifuge for an additional minute to remove impurities.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh microfuge tube to obtain the amplified eluate.
Titer the amplified phage as described in section 3.
Repeat sections 2 to 4 for the second round of biopanning.
Reduce the coating concentration of FGFR2 protein to 5 μg/mL.
Use the amplified phage from step 4.7 as input and keep the titer same as in the first round (10^11 PFU).
Shorten the incubation time of phage and FGFR2-coated dish to 1 h.
Increase the Tween concentration to 0.1% (v/v) in wash steps.
Repeat steps 2.1-2.6 for the third round of biopanning.
Elute bound phage by adding 1 mL of 20 μM bFGF solution to the dish and rocking gently for 60 min at room temperature.
Repeat steps 3.1-3.7.
Dilute an overnight culture of ER2738 in LB (1:100).
Dispense 1 mL of diluted culture into a 2 mL tube for each clone.
Pick one well-separated blue colored plaque from a titer plate and transfer to the tube containing the diluted culture.
Incubate the tubes with vigorous shaking for 4.5 h at 37 °C.
Transfer cultures to centrifuge tubes and centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 30 s.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube and centrifuge again.
Using a pipette, transfer the upper 80% of the supernatant to a fresh tube.
Label this as the amplified phage stock.
Dilute the amplified phage with an equal volume of 100% sterile glycerol and store at -80 °C for later use.
Transfer 500 μL of the amplified phage to a fresh microfuge tube.
Add a 1/6 volume of 20% PEG/2.5 M NaCl to the mixture.
Invert to mix and let it stand for 10–20 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Pour off the supernatant.
Centrifuge again if necessary.
Carefully remove any remaining supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet thoroughly in 100 μL of iodide buffer by vigorously tapping the tube.
Add 250 µL of 100% ethanol and incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant.
Wash the pellet with 0.5 mL of pre-cooled 70% ethanol.
Quickly centrifuge again.
Remove the supernatant.
Briefly dry the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 30 µL of TE buffer and use this for sequencing.
Degas sterile water using an ultrasonic instrument.
Dissolve the small peptide and the FGFR2 extracellular protein in sterile water.
Centrifuge these samples to remove residual precipitate.
Perform ITC titration experiments at 25 °C.
Titrate 40 μM of small peptide in the cell with 1.5 μM of FGFR2 protein from the syringe.
Stir at a speed of 750 rpm during the titration.
Add the FGRR2 protein in 2 μL aliquots (for a total of 19 injections).
Maintain 5-min intervals between each injection.
Analyze ITC data using a single-site binding model.
Seed BALB/c 3T3 cells at a density of 3.0 × 10^3 cells/well in a 96-well plate with DMEM containing 10% FBS overnight at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Replace the supernatant with fresh DMEM supplemented with 0.5% FBS and starve the cells for 12 h.
Make serial dilutions of the small peptide in DMEM supplemented with 0.5% FBS (concentrations: 0, 0.0064, 0.032, 0.16, 0.8, 4, 20, and 100 μM).
Add 100 μL of the small peptide solution per well to duplicate wells for each concentration.
Incubate the 96-well plate containing cells and peptides at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 48 h.
Replace supernatant with fresh DMEM containing 10% CCK-8 solution after incubation period.
Incubate the 96-well plate again at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 2 h.
Measure absorbance of each well at 450 nm using a microplate reader to analyze cell viability.
